plans.note: Only the preamble is exposed in the outline; a Master Services Agreement of this type will carry a limitation of liability article. Scan the body text captured under sec-preamble for cap language, mutuality and carve-outs (IP indemnity, confidentiality, gross negligence/willful misconduct).

Look within the sec-preamble text for a Kubient (Vendor) indemnity covering third-party IP infringement and its own negligence/misconduct, and confirm any AP-side indemnity is narrow. Treat as missing only if no indemnity language appears anywhere in the full text.

Presence check only. Non-competes restricting a customer are uncommon in an ad-tech MSA; sweep the sec-preamble text for 'shall not compete', 'competing service' or similar restraints on AP's businesses before concluding absence.

Presence check. Search for 'exclusive', 'sole provider', 'shall not engage any third party' in the operative text; ad-tech MSAs sometimes embed exclusivity in the services or inventory description, so read the scope language carefully.
Direction check. Look for 'most favoured/favored nation', 'no less favorable terms' in pricing or fee language. Flag only if the obligation runs against AP; an MFN in our favour is welcome.

Non-solicits frequently sit near confidentiality or general provisions. Check duration, whether it binds AP (or is mutual), and whether general advertising/unsolicited applicant carve-outs are present.

Defined term 'Initial Term' signals a term-and-termination article in the body. Verify AP has convenience termination on notice without penalty and that Kubient cannot terminate for convenience mid-term.
Tied to 'Initial Term'; examine the renewal mechanic for auto-renewal length, the non-renewal notice window (prefer 30 days or less) and any uncapped price uplift on renewal.

Standard boilerplate near the end of the body. Confirm the chosen law is NY/DE/CA/E&W and that disputes go to courts rather than foreign arbitration; Kubient is New York-based so NY is likely and acceptable.
Boilerplate assignment clause. Check AP can assign to affiliates and successors without consent, and that a change of control of AP does not give Kubient a termination or consent right.

Direction check on the IP/ownership article: AP must retain its content, data and any paid-for deliverables; flag any assignment or broad licence of AP data or feeds to Kubient beyond what is needed to deliver the services.

Review the grant to AP (platform/service access): confirm it extends to affiliates and contractors and is not revocable at Kubient's discretion. Note the two-way grant structure typical of ad-exchange agreements.

Check for audit or inspection rights over AP's usage or records (often near fees/reporting). Assess frequency, notice, on-site scope and who bears cost; audit rights running in AP's favour over Kubient's reporting are not flagged.
Direction check. Look for early-termination fees, penalties or liquidated damages payable by AP in the fees or termination language; service credits or make-good payments to AP are acceptable.
Examine the warranty article for a Kubient services warranty, its duration and remedy, and watch for an all-caps AS-IS/disclaimer that would gut it.
Kubient handles AP data through its platform, so insurance (including cyber/tech E&O) is expected. If no insurance covenant appears anywhere in the body, classify as missing.
Presence check on the fees/commercial terms: search for minimum spend, minimum volume, take-or-pay or shortfall true-up obligations on AP, and whether any such commitment has an exit.
Check the effects-of-termination/survival language for return or deletion of AP data and any transition assistance obligation; mark missing only if neither appears in the full body.
